_note: Themes are structure, not content. Membership is DERIVED: `keywords` are counted across each entry's own layer text, and an entry that clears `min_hits` joins the theme with an edge pointing at the layer where the discussion is. Nothing here decides on the reader's behalf which prophet is 'about patience' — the corpus text does. Definitions are one-line glosses of the kind found in any glossary of Islamic terms; anything longer waits for a cited source.
_thresholds: Every `min_hits` below was set by measuring the actual hit distribution across all 186 corpus entries (tools/audit_corpus.dart shows the method), not by guessing. Each one sits at the point where the curve falls away, so a theme collects the entries that discuss it and stops before the ones that mention the word in passing. A common English keyword needs a higher bar than a specific term, which is why 'leadership' — whose keywords include 'command' and 'appointed' — requires 5 while 'tawheed' requires 2. 'wisdom' was removed from `ilm` because hikmah is not 'ilm; keeping it pulled in divine-name pages that say events happen by Allah's wisdom, which is a different subject.

themes.title: Knowledge
themes.definition: Knowing, and the seeking of it — the first thing Adam was given and the first command of the revelation.

themes.title: Patience
themes.definition: Holding fast under difficulty without abandoning what is right.

themes.title: Repentance
themes.definition: Turning back — leaving a wrong, regretting it, and returning to Allah.

themes.title: Mercy
themes.definition: Mercy — the attribute the revelation opens with and returns to throughout.

themes.title: Tawheed
themes.definition: The oneness of Allah — the message every prophet was sent with.

themes.title: Leadership
themes.definition: Carrying responsibility for others — consultation, appointment, and answering for a trust.
